chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to me, saying: Al-Nu'man ibn Ahmad ibn Naeem al-Wasiti narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to me, saying: Mujalid narrated from al-Amr, from al-Masruq, saying:

A man came to Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and said: 'O Abu Abd al-Rahman, has your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) told you how many successors will be after him?' He replied: 'Yes. No one had asked me about it before you, and indeed you are the youngest of the people in age. Yes,' he said, 'There will be after me as many as the chiefs of the Israelites after Moses (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.أَحَدُثُ الْقَوْمِ سِنًّا: The youngest of the people in age

ai.seo_question: How many successors did the Prophet say would follow him according to the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal highlights the early recognition of the Twelve Imams by prominent companions like Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who links their leadership to the twelve chiefs (nuqaba') of the Israelites mentioned in the Quran. The comparison underscores the continuity of divine guidance and the specific number of authoritative leaders appointed after the Prophet, a key tenet in Shia theology regarding the Imamate.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 12-11 Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Qat’tan narrated that Al-Nue’man ibn Ahmad ibn Na’eem al-Vaseti quoted Ahmad ibn Senan al-Qat’tan on the authority of Abu Usamah, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Masruq,

“A man went to see Abdullah ibn Masood and asked him, ‘O Aba Abdul Rahman! Has your Prophet told you how many successors he will have after him?’ He replied, “Yes. No one had asked me this question before. You asked it although you are the youngest of them all. The Prophet (MGB) has said, ‘There will be twelve successors after me - as many as the Israelite chiefs after Moses (MGB).’”
